analogs.covers: Life: colony of females with a couple of males, beach basking, playful leaping, curious about land animals
Body and role: a gentle, long-necked glider that basks and ends up as the favourite prey of faster sea hunters

headline: A sea-lion colony in a long-necked, turtle-like body: basks on beaches, plays in the surf, hunts in turns.

setting.label: Open sea, coasts and beaches
setting.note: Nomadic aquatic. Swims near the surface and basks in shallows or briefly on land.

playsLike: You are a medium aquatic carnivore in a 'bale' of up to 6 females and 2 males. You are curious and friendly, fetching trinkets from the seafloor for land animals, but also a capable coordinated hunter: up to 3 take turns biting prey up to Large tier, starting with unattended Leedsichthys young and then Medium tier. You flee adult Spinosaurus and Deinosuchus, and Tylosaurus hunts you before anything else.

why.text: Up to 6 females and 2 males. Male duos drive off rival males and males fight each other for females. Sea lion colonies look the same.
Leaps out of the water in play and basks in shallow water or on land.
Approaches new species with curiosity and fetches objects from the seafloor to present to land animals.
Opportunistic, intelligent, coordinated: members take turns swimming in to bite.
Tylosaurus must hunt Kaiwhekea first and Eurhinosaurus torments it. Orcas hunt sea lions and turtles the same way. A group of turtles is also called a 'bale' (official inspiration: sea turtles).

notLike: Sea turtles don't hunt big prey; Kaiwhekea takes up to Large tier.
Sea lions haul out on land for long stretches; Kaiwhekea only basks on land for a short time.
